title: Modi to Meet Putin at SCO Summit in First Bilateral Since December
excerpt: India's PM begins a two-nation Central Asia tour Saturday, with bilateral meetings lined up alongside Putin and Xi Jinping at the 25th-anniversary SCO summit.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi will hold a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan, their first meeting since Putin's India visit in December 2025.
  • The summit marks the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, with Modi set to highlight India's priorities on security, connectivity, and economic opportunity.
  • Modi's two-nation Central Asia tour to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan begins Saturday, and he will also meet Chinese President Xi Jinping ahead of India's BRICS summit in September.
  • The meeting follows External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar's visit to Moscow this week, where Putin assured India of continued fertilizer supplies.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit later this week, the Indian government announced Thursday, in what will be their first bilateral engagement since Putin visited India in December 2025.

The SCO summit, taking place from August 31 to September 1, will be preceded by Modi's two-nation Central Asia tour to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan beginning Saturday. The visit carries diplomatic weight as the 25th anniversary of the Eurasian bloc, of which India has been a full member since 2017.

A Busy Diplomatic Calendar

Beyond the Putin bilateral, Modi will also come face to face with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the summit — a significant encounter ahead of India hosting the BRICS summit on September 12-13, where Xi is expected to attend.

"The Prime Minister will address the summit where he will highlight India's priorities of security, connectivity and opportunity at the forum," the Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement. "He will also hold bilateral meets with SCO leaders on the sidelines of the summit."

Modi will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games, a celebration of Central Asian cultural heritage being held in Kyrgyzstan.

Building on Jaishankar's Moscow Visit

The Modi-Putin meeting follows External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar's visit to Moscow this week for the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation. During the visit, Jaishankar also met directly with Putin.

"I would like to ask you to convey my very best wishes to Mr. Modi. I hope to see him in the near future, as we planned."

— Vladimir Putin, President of Russia, to EAM Jaishankar

During their discussions, Putin assured Jaishankar of continued supply of fertilizers to India, saying Russia is "doing everything to help Indian farmers." Trade, investment, energy, and nuclear cooperation were also on the agenda. Jaishankar told Putin that Modi is looking forward to hosting him for the BRICS summit in September.

India's SCO Balancing Act

The SCO summit presents India with both opportunities and diplomatic complexities. With Pakistan also a full member of the grouping, India is likely to use the platform to reiterate that the original SCO mandate was to combat terrorism, extremism, and separatism — a longstanding position that carries implicit messaging directed at Islamabad.

For the Indian diaspora closely watching New Delhi's geopolitical positioning, the summit offers a window into how India navigates its relationships with both Russia and China while maintaining its strategic autonomy. The Modi-Xi interaction will be particularly watched for signals on the trajectory of India-China ties following border disengagement and the gradual normalization of relations after the 2020 Galwan Valley standoff.

What to Watch

The bilateral meetings at the summit will set the tone for a packed diplomatic September, with the BRICS summit in India following just two weeks later. The outcomes of Modi's conversations with Putin on energy and defense cooperation, and any progress on the broader India-Russia trade relationship, will be closely watched by the diaspora business community.
